table.name: airlines
table.purpose: Lookup table of 12 US airlines, referenced by the flights table via a numeric id. Each row is one airline with its full name, short name, and country.

Abbreviation.name: airline_short_name
Abbreviation.description: Short/common brand name of the airline (e.g. 'AirTran', 'JetBlue', 'USAir'), one per row, unique across the 12 rows.

Airline.name: airline_full_name
Airline.description: Full legal/marketing name of the airline (e.g. 'US Airways', 'Southwest Airlines', 'JetBlue Airways'), unique per row.

Country.name: airline_country
Country.description: Country of the airline; constant 'USA' for all 12 rows, so it carries no discriminating information in this dataset.

uid.name: airline_id
uid.description: Numeric primary key (1-12) identifying the airline; referenced by flights.Airline as a many-to-one foreign key.

table.name: airports
table.purpose: Reference/lookup table of airports (one row per airport), used by the flights table as source and destination airport. All airports are in the United States; codes appear to be IATA-style 3-letter codes. Only 100 airports are included, likely a subset relevant to the flights data.

AirportCode.name: airport_code
AirportCode.description: Unique 3-letter airport code (IATA-style, e.g. ABQ, APN). Primary key of the table; referenced by flights.SourceAirport and flights.DestAirport.

AirportName.name: airport_name
AirportName.description: Name of the airport (e.g. 'Alpena County Regional', 'Phillips AAF'). Not unique; 12 rows share the generic name 'Municipal'. Values carry trailing spaces.

City.name: city
City.description: City where the airport is located (e.g. 'Alpena', 'Anchorage'). Not unique; several airports share a city.

Country.name: country
Country.description: Full country name; constant 'United States' for all rows.

CountryAbbrev.name: country_abbreviation
CountryAbbrev.description: Two-letter country code, 'US' in all rows; one row has a padded variant 'US ' (trailing space), so effectively constant.

table.name: flights
table.purpose: One row per flight: which airline operates it, its flight number, and the origin and destination airports (by airport code).

Airline.name: airline_id
Airline.description: Identifier of the operating airline; references airlines.uid (e.g. 2=USAir, 4=Southwest, 8=JetBlue, 11=Allegiant, 12=Virgin). 12 distinct airlines, each with 100 flights.

DestAirport.name: destination_airport_code
DestAirport.description: Destination airport, given as a 3-letter IATA/airport code (with a leading space) referencing airports.AirportCode (e.g. APN=Alpena County Regional).

FlightNo.name: flight_number
FlightNo.description: Airline flight number (integer, 2-1535). Not unique in the table since different airlines can share a flight number; together with Airline it likely identifies the flight.

SourceAirport.name: origin_airport_code
SourceAirport.description: Origin/departure airport, given as a 3-letter IATA/airport code (with a leading space) referencing airports.AirportCode.
